transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?
Hello. I'm here today because I have an intense, overwhelming fear of dogs. It has gotten to the point where I feel like I really need some help managing it.
Do you find yourself avoiding places or situations where you might encounter dogs due to your fear?

Yes, absolutely. I completely avoid going to local parks and even change my daily walking routes to make sure I don't run into any. I've also had to stop visiting friends who own dogs because the fear of encountering one is just too overwhelming for me.
How much does your fear of dogs interfere with your daily life, and are there any situations where you feel your fear is manageable or less intense?

It severely limits my daily life and social activities because I constantly have to avoid parks, specific streets, and visiting friends who have pets. The fear is only somewhat manageable if I am with a trusted companion or if the dog is securely leashed and far away, though I still feel highly anxious.
Is your fear specifically of all dogs, or is it more focused on certain breeds, sizes, or behaviors of dogs?
My fear is definitely directed toward all dogs in general. It doesn't matter what breed, size, or how friendly they seem; any dog triggers the exact same intense fear in me.
Can you tell me when your fear of dogs started, and if there was a specific incident or event that triggered it?
My fear of dogs started about a year and seven months ago. I honestly can't recall any specific incident or event that triggered it; it just seemed to develop around that time.
When you encounter a dog or even think about dogs, do you experience any physical symptoms such as a racing heart, sweating, trembling, or shortness of breath?

Yes, definitely. Whenever I see a dog, my heart races, I start sweating and trembling, and I feel like I can't breathe. Even just thinking about the possibility of running into one triggers that same intense anxiety and physical tension.
